display_title: Tijdelijke subsidieregeling vroege opschaling energietransitie zeeschepen 2026-2030: openstelling 2026 – Tijdelijke subsidieregeling vroege opschaling energietransitie zeeschepen 2026-2030
programme: Tijdelijke subsidieregeling vroege opschaling energietransitie zeeschepen 2026-2030
call_title: Tijdelijke subsidieregeling vroege opschaling energietransitie zeeschepen 2026-2030: openstelling 2026
executive_summary: First opening of a Dutch investment subsidy of the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management, run by RVO, for shipowners established in the Netherlands that buy and install a hydrogen or methanol energy line (propulsion system) in a new or retrofitted seagoing vessel, optionally with energy-saving techniques and a battery pack (each up to EUR 400,000). The subsidy is 40% of eligible costs, plus 10 percentage points for an emission-free vessel and 10 or 20 points for medium or small companies, up to EUR 4 million per project and one vessel per application. The budget is EUR 29 million of the scheme's EUR 102.8 million to 2029; it is a tender ranked on five criteria, open from 6 October 2026, 09:00, to 9 February 2027, 17:00. Projects must start within 6 months of the grant decision and be completed within 3 years.
status_rationale: The scheme (Staatscourant 2026, 21927, articles 1, 3 and 8; RVO page, Waarvoor krijgt u subsidie?) funds Dutch shipowners' purchase and installation of hydrogen or methanol energy lines on seagoing vessels, with optional onboard energy-saving techniques and battery packs. It does not touch TenneT's field: unlike the inland-shipping scheme it funds no shore-side charging or other grid-connected infrastructure, only onboard propulsion fuelled by bunkered hydrogen or methanol, and no project file is close. Both project dates are null because the call states only a start within 6 months of the grant decision and completion within 3 years.
